lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Buttons, Clicks & Keys'. Tour the ICT room, agree class rules, name the main parts of a computer (screen, keyboard, mouse, system unit) and switch on/log in safely.
lessons.sowResources: Interactive whiteboard, class-rules poster, printed parts-of-a-computer flashcards, BBC Bitesize KS1 'Parts of a Computer'. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Name the four main parts of a computer: screen, keyboard, mouse, system unit.
Log in to a school computer using my own class login card.
Say two ICT room rules in my own words.

plan.title: Welcome circle
plan.detail: Sit on the carpet. Show the ICT room: where to line up, where bags go, how to carry a chair. Term theme reveal: 'Buttons, Clicks & Keys'.

plan.title: Parts of a computer
plan.detail: Hold up the flashcards one at a time. Class repeats the word, then points to the real part on their own machine. Play 'Simon says point to the...'.

plan.title: Class rules together
plan.detail: Agree 4 rules: dry hands, walk not run, gentle hands on equipment, ask before printing. Each child signs the class-rules poster.

plan.title: First log in
plan.detail: Hand out login cards. Model on the big screen: type username, press Tab, type password, press Enter. Circulate - most will need the username typed with them.

plan.title: Log out and line up
plan.detail: Model the log-out routine. Everyone logs out, pushes in chairs, and says one part of the computer as the exit ticket.

activities: Login race in pairs (confident child supports partner)
successCriteria: I can point to the screen, keyboard, mouse and system unit.
I can log in with help and log out on my own.
I can name one ICT room rule.

resources.label: BBC Bitesize KS1 - Parts of a Computer

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise mouse control through short game-style activities. Learn point, single-click, double-click and click-and-drag.
lessons.sowResources: ABCya! Mouse Practice, ictgames.com 'Cursor Chaser', pixelthoughts.co 'Drag & Drop'. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Hold the mouse correctly with my hand resting on it.
Point and single-click on a target.
Double-click to open, and click-and-drag to move an object.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Sit tall, feet flat. Free-explore TypingClub while the class settles.

plan.title: Mouse grip demo
plan.detail: Big-screen demo: hand rests on the mouse, index finger on the left button, wrist on the desk. Everyone copies without clicking - 'ghost practice'.

plan.title: Click and double-click
plan.detail: ABCya! Mouse Practice: point-and-click level first, then the double-click level. Say the rhythm out loud: 'tap-tap, quick!'.

plan.title: Drag and drop
plan.detail: Move to a drag-and-drop puzzle game. Rule: press, hold, move, let go. Pair weaker mouse control with a confident partner.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Thumbs up / thumbs down: which was hardest - click, double-click or drag? Log-out routine.

successCriteria: I hold the mouse with my hand resting, not gripping.
I can single-click a small target first time.
I can drag an object where I want it.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Sign in to TypingClub with class logins. Teach good sitting posture and 'home row' hand position. Complete the first two beginner units.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub (typingclub.com), teacher-projected posture poster, class login cards. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson) — this IS the whole lesson today.
objectives: Sign in to TypingClub with my own class login.
Sit with good typing posture: back straight, feet flat, wrists up.
Put my fingers on the home row and complete two beginner units.

plan.title: Posture chant
plan.detail: Feet flat, back straight, elbows down, eyes on the screen. Practise the pose three times before anyone touches a keyboard.

plan.title: Sign in together
plan.detail: Login cards out. Model TypingClub sign-in on the big screen, one field at a time. Circulate - the first sign-in always takes longest.

plan.title: Home row hands
plan.detail: Show the two bumps on F and J. Everyone finds them with eyes closed. Left hand ASDF, right hand JKL. Repeat the chant.

plan.title: Units 1 and 2
plan.detail: Work through the first two beginner units. Freeze the class every 5 minutes for a posture check.

plan.title: Stars and log out
plan.detail: Everyone shows their star count to a partner. Praise accuracy, not speed. Log-out routine.

successCriteria: I can sign in to TypingClub with my card.
I can find F and J without looking.
I finished two units with my fingers on the home row.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Find and use the space bar, Enter and Backspace. Type single letters and their own first name.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub, printed keyboard mat, teacher name-card exemplar. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Find the space bar, Enter and Backspace on the keyboard.
Use Backspace to fix a mistake instead of asking for help.
Type my own first name correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Straight into TypingClub for 10 minutes. Posture check at 5 minutes.

plan.title: Keyboard treasure hunt
plan.detail: Call out a key - space bar, Enter, Backspace, Shift - children point to it on the printed keyboard mat, then on the real keyboard.

plan.title: Space, Enter, Backspace
plan.detail: Open a blank document. Type letters, press space, press Enter to go down a line. Deliberately type a wrong letter and fix it with Backspace - celebrate mistakes.

plan.title: Type my name
plan.detail: Type first name. Show how Shift makes the capital letter. Model with a name card. Type it three times, each one neater than the last.

plan.title: Show a partner
plan.detail: Partner checks: is the first letter a capital? Are the letters in the right order? Log out.

successCriteria: I can find the space bar, Enter and Backspace.
I fix my own typing mistakes with Backspace.
I can type my first name with a capital letter.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Open Tux Paint (or Microsoft Paint). Choose colours, use the Brush, Stamp and Fill tools to draw a picture, then save it to the class folder.
lessons.sowResources: Tux Paint (tuxpaint.org, free) OR Microsoft Paint, teacher gallery of exemplars. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Open Tux Paint (or Microsoft Paint) from the desktop.
Use the Brush, Stamp and Fill tools to make a picture.
Save my picture into the class folder.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes of TypingClub, posture check.

plan.title: Gallery inspiration
plan.detail: Show 3 exemplar pictures. Ask: which tool made this line? Which made this shape? Introduce today's prompt: 'my favourite place'.

plan.title: Tool tour
plan.detail: Demo Brush (choose colour, change size), Stamp (pick a picture, click to place) and Fill (click inside a shape). Children copy each step on their own screen.

plan.title: Create
plan.detail: Free creation time with the prompt. Circulate and name the tools out loud as children use them: 'you used the Fill tool there'.

plan.title: Save it
plan.detail: Model saving: File > Save, type first name, click Save. Everyone saves before the log-out routine.

successCriteria: I can open the painting program by myself.
I used at least two different tools in my picture.
My picture is saved with my name on it.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise the whole routine: log in -> open a program -> save with a sensible name -> close -> log out. Find yesterday's picture and reopen it.
lessons.sowResources: Windows File Explorer, class shared drive, printed step-by-step routine card. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Follow the whole computer routine: log in, open, save, close, log out.
Give my file a sensible name.
Find and reopen a picture I saved last week.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Routine card
plan.detail: Hand out the printed routine card. Read the 5 steps together as a chant: log in, open, save, close, log out.

plan.title: Find last week's picture
plan.detail: Open File Explorer, go to the class folder, find their own name, double-click to reopen. This is the trickiest part - pair up early finishers as helpers.

plan.title: Add and re-save
plan.detail: Add one new thing to the picture, then Save again. Discuss: the file keeps the same name, the picture is updated.

plan.title: Routine race
plan.detail: Timed run through the full 5-step routine. Everyone claps for the class, not individuals. Log out.

successCriteria: I can find my own file in the class folder.
I save my work with a name that makes sense.
I can do the whole routine with one reminder or fewer.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Discuss 'if something feels wrong, tell a trusted adult'. Learn one class rule: keep private things (name, address, photos) private.
lessons.sowResources: ThinkUKnow 'Jessie & Friends' Ep. 1 (thinkuknow.co.uk), story book 'Chicken Clicking' by Jeanne Willis. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain that some things are private: my name, my address and my photos.
Say what to do if something online feels wrong - tell a trusted adult.
Name one trusted adult I could tell.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Jessie & Friends
plan.detail: Watch ThinkUKnow 'Jessie & Friends' Episode 1. Pause at the decision point and ask: what should she do?

plan.title: Private or share?
plan.detail: Sorting game: hold up cards (my favourite colour / my home address / my pet's name / my school photo). Class votes private or okay-to-share, then discuss.

plan.title: Trusted adults hand
plan.detail: Draw round a hand; write or draw a trusted adult on each finger. This goes into the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Class promise
plan.detail: Say the class online-safety rule together: 'If something feels wrong, I tell a trusted adult.' Log out.

successCriteria: I can name two things that should stay private.
I know to tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong.
I can name at least one trusted adult.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Print or save the best Paint picture into the personal portfolio folder. Show it to a partner and say one thing they are proud of.
lessons.sowResources: Tux Paint / Paint, class printer, printed portfolio cover sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose my best piece of work and say why it is my best.
Save or print it into my portfolio folder.
Tell a partner one thing I am proud of.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Choosing my best
plan.detail: Open the class folder and look at all their pictures. Sentence stem on the board: 'I chose this one because...'.

plan.title: Tidy it up
plan.detail: Open the chosen picture and improve one thing - a colour, a missing detail, a title stamp. Save it again.

plan.title: Into the portfolio
plan.detail: Print (or save to the portfolio folder). Stick the printed cover sheet on the front and write their name on it.

plan.title: Proud partners
plan.detail: Turn to a partner: 'I am proud of... because...'. Two or three share with the whole class. Log out.

successCriteria: I chose a piece of work and gave a reason.
My work is in my portfolio folder with my name.
I told a partner one thing I am proud of.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Rotate through 4 short stations: mouse game, TypingClub, Paint drawing, log-in-and-save race. Teacher observes and ticks off the skills checklist.
lessons.sowResources: Skills checklist per pupil, station cards, timer. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Move sensibly between four ICT stations.
Show the skills I have learned this term without being told each step.
Ask for help using words, not just a raised hand.

plan.title: Station briefing
plan.detail: Explain the four stations and the rotation signal (timer bell). Groups of 4-5, 12 minutes per station.

plan.title: Station 1 - Mouse game
plan.detail: Click and drag accuracy game. Observe grip and control, tick the checklist.

plan.title: Station 2 - TypingClub
plan.detail: Independent unit work. Observe posture and home-row hand position.

plan.title: Station 3 - Paint
plan.detail: Free drawing with at least two tools. Observe tool choice and independence.

plan.title: Station 4 - Log in and save race
plan.detail: Full routine from log-in to save. Observe who still needs the routine card.

plan.title: Checklist reveal
plan.detail: Show each child their ticked checklist. Name one thing to practise next week. Log out.

successCriteria: I moved between stations quietly when the timer went.
I did each station task without step-by-step help.
I know one thing to practise next week.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Whole-class recap: name the parts, log in, open a program, save, log out. Rehearse the practical task in pairs.
lessons.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Recall the parts of the computer and the log-in routine.
Complete the practical task steps in the right order.
Say one online-safety rule out loud, clearly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Quickfire recap
plan.detail: Slide recap: point to the part, name it, chant the 5-step routine, say the safety rule together.

plan.title: Rehearse the practical
plan.detail: In pairs, one child does the exam task while the partner reads the task card aloud, then swap. Task: log in, open Paint, draw a guided picture, save with own name, log out.

plan.title: Trouble spots
plan.detail: Reteach the two steps most children fumbled - usually saving with the right name, and finding the program icon.

plan.title: Safety rule rehearsal
plan.detail: Each child practises saying their safety rule to a partner in one clear sentence. Log out.

successCriteria: I can do the practical steps in order with a partner reading them.
I can save a file with my own name.
I can say one online-safety rule in a full sentence.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual observation: log in, open Paint, complete a short guided drawing, save the file with own name, log out. Answer one online-safety question aloud.
lessons.sowResources: Observation checklist (from HTML curriculum: 'logs in, controls the mouse, saves a picture; gives one online-safety rule out loud'), assessment rubric.
objectives: Complete the Term 1 practical task on my own.
Save my work with my own name.
Answer one online-safety question out loud.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start. Explain: this is a 'show me what you can do' task, not a test to worry about. Everyone gets a turn.

plan.title: Group A practical
plan.detail: First group works through the task while the rest do independent TypingClub. Observe against the checklist.

plan.title: Group B practical
plan.detail: Second group. Same task, same checklist.

plan.title: Group C practical
plan.detail: Third group. Same task, same checklist.

plan.title: Safety question + close
plan.detail: One-to-one: 'Tell me one rule for staying safe online.' Record the answer. Praise every child by name.

activities: Individual observed practical: log in, open Paint, guided drawing, save, log out
successCriteria: I logged in by myself.
I controlled the mouse to complete the drawing.
I saved the picture with my name and logged out.
I gave one online-safety rule out loud.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Plan a 4-page 'All About Me' picture book. Sketch on paper first: page 1 = my name, page 2 = my family, page 3 = my pet or favourite toy, page 4 = things I like.
lessons.sowResources: Printed storyboard sheet, coloured pencils. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Plan a 4-page book before I start on the computer.
Decide what goes on each page.
Sketch my ideas on the storyboard sheet.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Look at a real book
plan.detail: Share a simple picture book. Notice: each page has one idea and one picture. Show the finished teacher exemplar of 'My First Digital Book'.

plan.title: The four pages
plan.detail: Page 1 = my name. Page 2 = my family. Page 3 = my pet or favourite toy. Page 4 = things I like. Write the four headings on the board.

plan.title: Storyboard time
plan.detail: Sketch all four pages on paper with coloured pencils. No computers this lesson - planning first is the whole point. Circulate and ask 'what will you draw here?'.

plan.title: Tell your plan
plan.detail: Partners describe their four pages to each other. Collect storyboards in for next week.

successCriteria: My storyboard has all four pages sketched.
Each page has one clear idea.
I can tell a partner what each page will show.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Use Tux Paint / Paint to draw each of the 4 pages. Save each drawing with a clear name: page1.png, page2.png etc.
lessons.sowResources: Tux Paint / Paint, class shared drive. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Draw each page of my book using the paint tools.
Save each page with a clear name: page1, page2, page3, page4.
Follow my own plan from last week.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Plans back out
plan.detail: Return the storyboards. Model naming: page1, page2 - no capitals, no spaces. Write the naming rule on the board.

plan.title: Draw and save
plan.detail: Draw page by page, saving each one before starting the next. Rule on the board: 'finish a page, save a page'. Most children manage 2-3 pages today.

plan.title: Check the folder
plan.detail: Open the class folder and check the file names are right. Fix any that are wrong together. Log out.

successCriteria: My drawings match my plan.
Each page is saved separately.
My file names follow the page1, page2 rule.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Open a blank Word document. Type a one-line title under each page. Use the Shift key for the capital letter at the start.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Word, keyboard mat, teacher exemplar page. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Open a blank Word document.
Type a one-line title for each page.
Use the Shift key to make a capital letter at the start.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Shift key demo
plan.detail: Show the exemplar title page. Demo: hold Shift, press the letter, let go. Practise 'A a A a' in the air, then on screen.

plan.title: Open Word and set up
plan.detail: Open a blank document, type name at the top, press Enter twice. Model on the big screen at pupil pace.

plan.title: Type the four titles
plan.detail: One title per line, each starting with a capital. Backspace to fix mistakes. Support: printed title strips to copy from.

plan.title: Save and share
plan.detail: Save as titles.docx into their folder. Partner reads the titles aloud to check they make sense. Log out.

successCriteria: I opened a new Word document by myself.
I typed a title for each of my four pages.
Each title starts with a capital letter.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Present the finished picture book to a small group. Give one 'star' (something you liked) to a friend. Save the completed portfolio.
lessons.sowResources: Class projector, printed star stickers, portfolio folder. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Present my digital book to a small group.
Give a friend one 'star' - something I liked about their book.
Save my finished work into the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Rehearse with a partner
plan.detail: Practise the sentence: 'This is my book. My favourite page is ___ because ___.'

plan.title: Show and tell
plan.detail: Groups of five at the projector or around a screen. Each child gets two minutes. Audience sits with hands still and eyes on the speaker.

plan.title: Star stickers
plan.detail: After each presenter, one listener gives a star: 'I liked ___'. Everyone gets at least one star sticker.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save all four pages plus the titles document into the portfolio folder. Check the folder together on the big screen.

plan.title: Term celebration
plan.detail: Look back at Week 1. Name three things they can do now that they could not in August. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my book using two full sentences.
I gave a friend a kind, specific compliment.
All my work is in my portfolio folder.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Term theme: 'Typing & Documents'. Recap logging in, saving and the ICT room rules. Introduce this term's goal: type a formatted paragraph and save it in BOTH Word and Google Docs.
lessons.sowResources: Term overview slide, class-rules poster, TypingClub sign-in cards. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Log in and open a program without step-by-step help.
Explain what we will make this term: a formatted document saved in two places.
Set my own TypingClub target for the term.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Sign in, posture check, free practice while the class settles.

plan.title: Term reveal
plan.detail: Term theme: 'Typing & Documents'. Show the finished exemplar fact card they will make by Week 15. Explain the two-tool idea: Microsoft AND Google.

plan.title: Rules and routine recap
plan.detail: Recap the ICT room rules and the 5-step routine from Year 1. Quickfire: who can log in, open Word and close it in under 2 minutes?

plan.title: Diagnostic task
plan.detail: Type one sentence about the holidays, save it with own name. Note who needs support with typing, saving or the mouse - this sets the groupings for the term.

plan.title: My target
plan.detail: Each pupil writes their TypingClub target on the goal sheet (a star count or a level). Stick to the wall chart. Log out.

successCriteria: I logged in and opened a program on my own.
I typed and saved a sentence with my name on it.
I have written my typing target on the chart.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Focus on home-row rhythm and accuracy — quality before speed. Aim to finish TypingClub Level 1 by half term.
lessons.sowResources: TypingClub, wall chart of class accuracy stars. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Keep my fingers on the home row while typing.
Choose accuracy before speed.
Reach the end of TypingClub Level 1 by half term.

plan.title: Hands ready
plan.detail: F and J bumps, elbows down, eyes on screen. 60-second warm-up drill on the home row only.

plan.title: Rhythm, not race
plan.detail: Model typing slowly with an even beat, then fast and messy. Ask which one scored better. Rule for the term: 'smooth beats fast'.

plan.title: TypingClub units
plan.detail: Independent unit work towards Level 1. Freeze for a posture check every 5 minutes. Support: cover hands with a card for children who peek.

plan.title: Accuracy stars
plan.detail: Each pupil records today's best accuracy on the wall chart. Celebrate anyone above 90% regardless of speed.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Which letter is hardest to reach? Show it on the keyboard mat and practise ten times. Log out.

successCriteria: My fingers start and return to the home row.
My accuracy is 90% or better in at least one lesson.
I typed without looking down for a whole exercise.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.subtopic: Word vs Google Docs — A Quick Tour
lessons.outline: Open both Microsoft Word and Google Docs. Compare: same job, two tools. Type own name in each and save.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Word (school licence), Google Docs (Google Workspace for Education, free), Drive vs OneDrive comparison poster. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Open both Microsoft Word and Google Docs.
Explain that two different tools can do the same job.
Type and save my name in each one.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Two tools, one job
plan.detail: Side-by-side on the big screen: Word and Docs. Spot the same buttons in both. Analogy: two shops that both sell bread.

plan.title: Word first
plan.detail: Open Word, type full name, make it big, save to OneDrive as name_word.docx. Model each step, pupils copy.

plan.title: Then Docs
plan.detail: Open Docs in the browser, type the same name. Notice: Docs saves by itself - there is no Save button. Rename the document to name_docs.

plan.title: Spot the difference
plan.detail: Class list: what was the same, what was different? Record on the comparison poster. Log out.

activities: Type and rename in Google Docs
successCriteria: I opened Word and Google Docs by myself.
I typed my name in both.
I can say one difference between them.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Type a 3-4 sentence paragraph about 'My Weekend' in both Word and Docs. Use full stops and the space bar correctly.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, printed prompt card, teacher exemplar paragraph. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Type a paragraph of 3-4 sentences.
Use full stops and single spaces correctly.
Save the same paragraph in Word and in Docs.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What makes a sentence
plan.detail: Read the exemplar 'My Weekend' paragraph. Count the sentences, spot the capital letters and full stops.

plan.title: Plan out loud
plan.detail: Talk partners: say your three sentences before typing them. Prompt card: Who? Where? What did you do? How did you feel?

plan.title: Type it twice
plan.detail: Type the paragraph in Word, then copy the same into Docs. Rule: one space after a full stop, capital letter at the start of each sentence.

plan.title: Partner proofread
plan.detail: Swap seats and check a partner's paragraph for capitals and full stops. Fix and re-save. Log out.

activities: 'My Weekend' paragraph in Word and Docs
successCriteria: My paragraph has 3 or more sentences.
Every sentence starts with a capital and ends with a full stop.
The paragraph is saved in both Word and Docs.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Highlight and format text. Make important words Bold, use Italic for a title, Underline a keyword. Save the updated file.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, formatting-toolbar cheat sheet, teacher demo. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Highlight text with the mouse or Shift + arrows.
Apply Bold, Italic and Underline.
Explain why we make some words stand out.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why format?
plan.detail: Show the same paragraph plain and formatted. Which is easier to read? Rule: formatting helps the reader, it is not decoration.

plan.title: Highlight first
plan.detail: The hard part is selecting text. Practise three ways: click-drag, double-click a word, Shift + arrow keys. Everyone selects the same three words.

plan.title: B, I, U
plan.detail: Open last week's paragraph. Make two important words Bold, the title Italic, one keyword Underlined. Same again in the Docs copy.

plan.title: Gallery check
plan.detail: Show three screens on the projector. Ask: is the formatting helping or shouting? Save and log out.

activities: Bold / Italic / Underline on own paragraph
successCriteria: I can select exactly the words I want.
I used bold, italic and underline for a reason.
My changes are saved in both files.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Change the font family, size and colour of a title and the body text. Discuss what looks readable and what does not.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, colour theory poster (contrast basics). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Change the font, size and colour of text.
Choose colours that are easy to read.
Say why yellow text on white is a bad choice.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Readable or not?
plan.detail: Show five colour combinations on the board. Vote readable / not readable. Introduce the word contrast.

plan.title: Font, size, colour
plan.detail: Demo the three dropdowns. Make the title 24pt in a dark colour, the body 12pt in black. Pupils copy on their paragraph.

plan.title: Design challenge
plan.detail: Make the paragraph look good with a maximum of two fonts and two colours. Constraint teaches restraint.

plan.title: Swap and rate
plan.detail: Partner rates readability out of 3. One improvement suggested and applied. Save, log out.

successCriteria: I changed the font, size and colour of my text.
My text is easy to read from a metre away.
I used no more than two fonts.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Insert a picture from a folder of copyright-safe images. Use the corner handles to resize; drag to position.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, class picture folder (Pixabay / Pexels pre-downloaded), image-handles handout. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Insert a picture from a folder into my document.
Resize a picture using the corner handles.
Move a picture to where I want it.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Corner handles rule
plan.detail: Demo stretching a photo from the side (squashed face) versus the corner (still correct). Rule: always drag the corner.

plan.title: Insert a picture

Correct my posture without being reminded.

Update the contents list after editing the document.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up

Format a header row.
Merge two cells to make a title row.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: When to use a table
plan.detail: Show the same data as a paragraph and as a table. Tables are for data with repeating fields, not for layout.

Header row styling and cell merge

The columns are wide enough for their content.
I merged cells to make a title row.

lessons.subject: ICT

objectives: Insert an image and add a caption using Insert Caption.
Explain why automatic figure numbering is better than typing numbers.
Keep captions consistent across the document.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Figure numbering
plan.detail: Show a report with Figure 1, 2, 3. Insert a new image in the middle - automatic numbering renumbers everything, manual does not.

plan.title: Insert Caption
plan.detail: Right-click image > Insert Caption (Word) or use the caption workaround in Docs. Add three captioned images.

plan.title: Caption style
plan.detail: Captions should be short, in a smaller size, and say what the figure shows - not 'picture of a dog' but 'Figure 2: a guide dog in training'.

plan.title: Consistency check
plan.detail: Partner checks all captions look and read the same way. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My images have captions with figure numbers.
The numbering updates when I add an image.
All my captions are styled the same way.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add a running header (report title), a footer (own name) and automatic page numbers.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, headers/footers handout. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add a running header with the report title.
Add a footer with my name.
Insert automatic page numbers.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why headers exist
plan.detail: Drop a printed report on the floor and mix the pages. Without page numbers and a header, reassembling is guesswork.

plan.title: Header and footer
plan.detail: Insert > Header: report title. Insert > Footer: own name. Show that editing one page changes all of them.

plan.title: Page numbers
plan.detail: Insert automatic page numbers in the footer, aligned right. Add 'Page X of Y' if the class is confident.

plan.title: Print preview
plan.detail: Check in print preview that headers and numbers appear on every page. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My header shows the report title on every page.
My footer shows my name.
Page numbers are automatic, not typed.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Use indents, line spacing and paragraph spacing to make text easy to read. Compare 'wall of text' vs a spaced-out version.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, before/after handout of spacing. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use line and paragraph spacing to make text readable.
Use indents correctly.
Compare a wall of text with a well-spaced version.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Wall of text
plan.detail: Project the before/after handout. Same words, different spacing. Ask which one they would actually read.

plan.title: Spacing controls
plan.detail: Demo line spacing (1.15 or 1.5), space after paragraph (6-10pt), and first-line indent. Change one at a time so the effect is visible.

plan.title: Apply to the report
plan.detail: Apply consistent spacing to the whole draft. Rule: set it once for the whole document, do not press Enter twice.

plan.title: Readability rating
plan.detail: Partner rates the page out of 5 for readability and suggests one change. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My line spacing is consistent throughout.
I used paragraph spacing instead of blank lines.
My page looks readable from arm's length.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Use spellcheck and grammar suggestions wisely — the underline is a hint, not always the fix. Discuss when to accept and when to ignore.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, printed proofreading checklist, examples of 'wrong wrong' vs 'wrong right' suggestions. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use spellcheck and grammar suggestions with judgement.
Explain when to ignore a suggestion.
Proofread using a checklist as well as the software.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The tool is not always right
plan.detail: Work through examples where the suggestion is wrong: names, Malaysian place names, technical words, 'their/there'. Discuss each.

plan.title: Run the checks
plan.detail: Run spellcheck and grammar check on the report draft. For each flag, decide: accept, ignore, or fix differently. Log three decisions on paper.

plan.title: Human proofread
plan.detail: Use the printed checklist for the things software misses: missing words, wrong figure numbers, headings out of order.

plan.title: Share a catch
plan.detail: Who found an error the software missed? Share it. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I checked every flag rather than clicking accept-all.
I can give an example of a suggestion I correctly ignored.
I found at least one error the software missed.

Apply the heading structure from the plan.
Meet the draft deadline.

plan.title: Plan review

plan.title: Draft
plan.detail: Type the report body and apply headings as you go. Target: 2 pages of text by the end of the lesson. Circulate with individual targets.

plan.title: Draft check
plan.detail: Navigation pane check: is the structure right? Word count check: is it long enough? Save and log out.

successCriteria: My draft covers all the sections in my plan.
All headings use real styles.
My draft reaches about two pages.

lessons.outline: Add TOC, a table, a captioned image and header/footer to the draft. Peer-check against the marking rubric.

Check my report against the marking rubric.
Fix everything the rubric says is missing.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Rubric walk-through
plan.detail: Read the marking rubric line by line. Pupils highlight anything they have not done yet.

plan.title: Complete the features
plan.detail: Work through the missing features: contents list, one table, one captioned image, header, footer, page numbers.

plan.title: Peer rubric check
plan.detail: Swap and mark your partner's report against the rubric. Give a score and one specific fix.

plan.title: Fix list
plan.detail: Write your top three fixes for next lesson on a sticky note. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My report has a TOC, a table, a captioned image and a header/footer.
I marked a partner's work fairly against the rubric.
I know my three biggest fixes.

Include an automatic contents list, one table and one captioned image.
Save with the correct file name.

plan.detail: Read the task twice before starting. Rubric on the board. Silent conditions, technical help only.

plan.detail: Set headings first, then type the body. Remind at 20 minutes: structure before decoration.

plan.title: Table and image
plan.detail: Insert the table with a header row and the captioned image.

plan.title: TOC, header, footer
plan.detail: Generate the contents list last so it picks up all headings. Add header, footer and page numbers.

plan.title: Save and close
plan.detail: Correct file name, saved to the assessment folder, checked before logging out.

activities: Contents list, table and captioned image
successCriteria: My report is two pages and uses heading styles.
My contents list was generated automatically.
I included one table and one captioned image.
The file is saved with the correct name.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Return to the mini report. Add a second table and a second image. Improve the introduction and conclusion.

objectives: Add a second table and a second image to my report.
Rewrite my introduction and conclusion.
Make sure the contents list still matches.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Strong openings
plan.detail: Compare two introductions: one that says 'This report is about dogs', one that opens with a fact. Rewrite yours to hook the reader.

plan.title: Add content
plan.detail: Insert a second table and a second captioned image where they add value, not just to fill space.

plan.title: Conclusion
plan.detail: Write a conclusion that answers the question the introduction raised. Three to four sentences.

plan.title: Update the TOC
plan.detail: Refresh the contents list and check page numbers. Save and log out.

activities: Add a second table and image
successCriteria: My introduction hooks the reader.
My report has two tables and two captioned images.
My contents list is up to date.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Learn to reference the table and figure numbers in the body text (e.g. 'see Figure 1'). Rebuild the TOC after edits.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, cross-reference how-to (Microsoft Support docs). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Refer to a table or figure by its number in the body text.
Use a cross-reference so it updates automatically.
Rebuild the contents list after edits.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why cross-reference
plan.detail: Show 'see Figure 1' typed by hand, then insert a new figure - the reference is now wrong. Show the cross-reference updating itself.

plan.title: Insert cross-references
plan.detail: References > Cross-reference. Add at least two references in the body text: 'as shown in Figure 2' and 'see Table 1'.

plan.title: Test it
plan.detail: Insert a new figure above the others, update fields, and watch every reference renumber.

plan.title: Rebuild the TOC
plan.detail: Update the contents list, check the page numbers, save and log out.

successCriteria: My body text refers to at least two figures or tables.
My references update automatically.
My contents list is correct after all edits.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Swap reports with a partner. Use tracked changes / suggesting mode to suggest 3 improvements. Author accepts / rejects.
lessons.sowResources: Word 'Track Changes' / Docs 'Suggesting mode', peer-editing guide. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Suggest three improvements using tracked changes or suggesting mode.
Accept or reject suggestions on my own work with a reason.
Explain the difference between editing and suggesting.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Suggesting vs editing
plan.detail: Demo both modes. Key idea: a suggestion asks, an edit takes. The author stays in charge.

plan.title: Peer edit
plan.detail: Swap reports. Turn on Track Changes / Suggesting mode. Make three specific suggestions - not 'make it better'.

plan.title: Accept or reject
plan.detail: Back to your own report. For each suggestion, accept or reject and say why to your partner. Rejecting with a good reason is a success, not a failure.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Which suggestion improved the report most? Save and log out.

successCriteria: I made three specific suggestions on a partner's report.
I accepted or rejected each suggestion on mine with a reason.
I can explain the difference between suggesting and editing.

resources.label: Word Track Changes / Docs Suggesting mode

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Export as PDF, save to the term portfolio folder, and present the report to a small group in 2 minutes.

objectives: Export my report as a PDF.
Present my report to a small group in two minutes.
Save the final version to the term portfolio folder.

plan.title: Final checks
plan.detail: Last pass: update the TOC, check page numbers, check every figure has a caption.

plan.title: Export to PDF
plan.detail: Save as PDF with the correct file name. Open the PDF to check nothing has shifted.

plan.title: Two-minute presentations
plan.detail: Small groups. Structure: what my report is about, one thing I found out, the feature I am proudest of. Timer strictly enforced.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: PDF and source document into the term portfolio folder.

plan.title: Term reflection
plan.detail: Name the report feature that was hardest and the one you will use again. Log out.

successCriteria: My PDF looks the same as my document.
I presented within the two-minute limit.
My final report is in the portfolio folder.

Describe what a micro:bit is and what it can do.
Explain what the term project will be.

plan.detail: Sign in, baseline WPM run, posture check.

plan.title: Unboxing the micro:bit
plan.detail: Pass round a micro:bit. Do not plug anything in yet - handling rules first: hold by the edges, never by the pins, no bending.

plan.title: What could we build?
plan.detail: Show short clips of finished projects: step counter, reaction game, light meter. Class brainstorms what the device must sense to do each one.

plan.title: Baseline and goal
plan.detail: Record baseline WPM. Set a personal goal on the goal sheet - realistic, about +5 WPM by half term.

plan.title: Term map
plan.detail: Walk through the term: blocks first, then loops, then conditions, then build a gadget. Log out.

successCriteria: I can handle a micro:bit safely.
I recorded my baseline WPM and set a goal.
I can name two things a micro:bit can sense.

lessons.outline: Explore the micro:bit hardware: LEDs, buttons, sensors (light, temp, accelerometer). Identify inputs vs outputs on a labelling sheet.

Sort features into inputs and outputs.
Explain the difference between an input and an output.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Input or output?

plan.title: Quickfire
plan.detail: Teacher names a part, class shouts input or output. Devices counted back in. Log out.

I sorted the features into inputs and outputs.
I can explain the difference in my own words.

Drag blocks to show an icon on the LED display.
Download my program onto the micro:bit.

activities: Show icon and download to device

I downloaded it onto the physical micro:bit.
I have seen my program written as Python text.

Explain in my own words what a loop does.
Build an LED animation using a loop.

lessons.subject: ICT

lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, printed dev-diary template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add one improvement to my gadget.
Record the change in a dev diary.
Explain why I chose that improvement.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Read the feedback
plan.detail: Re-read last week's tester feedback. Choose ONE improvement that fixes a real problem, not just a decoration.

plan.title: Implement one change
plan.detail: Add the improvement: a sound effect, a reset button, a start-up animation, or clearer output. Keep v1 saved - save this as v2.

plan.title: Dev diary
plan.detail: Complete the diary entry: what I changed, why, and whether it worked.

plan.title: Show the difference
plan.detail: Demo v1 then v2 to the pair who tested it. Log out.

successCriteria: My gadget has one clear improvement.
My dev diary explains what and why.
Both v1 and v2 are saved.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise explaining code to a partner using the sentence stems: 'This block means…', 'This loop repeats…', 'This if-block checks…'. Prepare for the exam.
lessons.sowResources: Sentence-stem cards, peer-explanation checklist, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain my code to a partner using the sentence stems.
Point out where the loop and the condition are.
Answer a question about my code without reading from the screen.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Model a good explanation
plan.detail: Teacher explains a sample program using the stems: 'This block means...', 'This loop repeats...', 'This if-block checks...'. Then a deliberately vague version - class spots the difference.

plan.title: Explain in pairs
plan.detail: Two rounds: explain your code to a partner, get scored on the peer checklist, then swap. Second round should be noticeably better.

plan.title: Teacher questions
plan.detail: Circulate asking one exam-style question each: 'What happens if I remove this block?', 'Where does the program start?'

plan.title: Weak spots
plan.detail: Each pupil notes the question they found hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I explained my whole program using the sentence stems.
I can point to the loop and the condition.
I answered a question about my code without reading it out.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual practical: build a small micro:bit program using at least one loop and one condition. Demonstrate it working; explain the code to the teacher.
lessons.sowResources: Marking rubric — from HTML: 'a working micro:bit gadget in Python using at least one loop and one condition'.
objectives: Build a micro:bit program using at least one loop and one condition.
Demonstrate it working on the physical device.
Explain my code to the teacher.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read the task. Requirements on the board: at least one loop, at least one condition, must run on the device.

plan.title: Build
plan.detail: Individual build (paired devices, individual code). Silent conditions. Technical help only - no design help.

plan.title: Demonstrate
plan.detail: Called one at a time to demo the working device while others continue or extend.

plan.title: Explain
plan.detail: One-to-one: point to your loop, point to your condition, say what each does. Recorded on the rubric.

plan.title: Save and close
plan.detail: Save the .hex with the correct name. Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses at least one loop.
My program uses at least one condition.
It runs on the physical micro:bit.
I explained my code clearly.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Learn 'radio send' and 'radio receive' blocks. Two micro:bits send a heart to each other when a button is pressed.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits per pair, radio-blocks reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Use radio send and radio receive blocks.
Set the same radio group on both devices.
Send a message from one micro:bit to another.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: How radio works
plan.detail: Both micro:bits must be on the same radio group - like tuning two walkie-talkies to the same channel. Assign each pair a group number to avoid chaos.

plan.title: Send and receive
plan.detail: Program: on start set radio group; on button A, radio send number 1; on radio received, show heart. Flash BOTH devices with the same program.

plan.title: Troubleshoot
plan.detail: Common faults: different group numbers, only one device flashed, battery not connected. Work through the fault-finding list together.

plan.title: Pair up across the room
plan.detail: Test how far apart the devices still work. Log out.

successCriteria: Both my micro:bits are on the same radio group.
Pressing a button on one shows something on the other.
I can name one reason radio might not work.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Extend the radio project: send different messages for buttons A, B and A+B. Display the received message on the second micro:bit.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits per pair, project brief. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Send different messages for buttons A, B and A+B.
Display the received message clearly.
Test my chat gadget with another pair.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Message plan
plan.detail: Decide what each button means: A = yes, B = no, A+B = hello. Write the code table on paper first.

plan.title: Build the chat gadget
plan.detail: Three send events, and a receive handler that shows the right icon or string for each value. This needs an if/else if chain - link back to Week 6.

plan.title: Cross-pair test
plan.detail: Swap one device with another pair on the same group and hold a conversation. Log out.

successCriteria: My gadget sends three different messages.
The receiving device shows the right thing for each.
Another pair could understand my messages.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Test the radio chat with another pair. Fix bugs. Add one polish feature (icon animation, sound, low-battery warning).
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits, bug log template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Find and fix at least one bug in my project.
Log the bug and the fix.
Add one polish feature.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Test properly
plan.detail: Test with another pair using a test list: press each button, press two at once, press very fast, move out of range. Log what breaks.

plan.title: Fix the bugs
plan.detail: Work through the bug log. Fix one at a time and re-test after each fix - not all at once.

plan.title: One polish feature
plan.detail: Add an icon animation, a sound, or a startup message. Save as v3.

plan.title: Bug of the week
plan.detail: Share the most interesting bug found and how it was fixed. Log out.

successCriteria: I tested my gadget against a test list.
I fixed at least one bug and logged it.
My gadget has one polish feature.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Set up a 'gadget fair': each pair demos their gadget for 2 minutes at a table. Save the final .hex to the portfolio folder.
lessons.sowResources: Class tables set up as demo stations, portfolio folder, visitors' feedback slips. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Demonstrate my gadget to visitors for two minutes.
Answer questions about how it works.
Save my final code to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Set up the fair
plan.detail: Tables become demo stations. Each pair sets out their device, a plan sheet and their dev diary.

plan.title: Rehearse the pitch
plan.detail: Structure: what it does, how to use it, how it works inside, what we would add next.

plan.title: Gadget fair
plan.detail: Half the class demos while half visits, then swap. Visitors leave a feedback slip at each station.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save the final .hex plus a photo of the device to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Reflection
plan.detail: One thing that went wrong and how you solved it. Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: I demoed my gadget within two minutes.
I answered a question about how it works.
My final .hex is in the portfolio folder.

lessons.outline: Term theme: 'micro:bit Python Projects'. Set a personal WPM goal in TypingClub. Preview the term project: a multi-feature micro:bit build.

objectives: Set a personal WPM goal for the term.
Recall what I built with the micro:bit in Year 5.
Describe this term's multi-feature project.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: Baseline WPM run, posture check.

plan.title: Year 5 recall
plan.detail: Quickfire: what does a loop do? What does an if-block do? What is an input? Pupils write answers on whiteboards - this shows what needs reteaching in Week 2.

plan.title: Project preview
plan.detail: Theme: 'micro:bit Python Projects'. Show last year's exemplar builds. This term the project must have at least three features and use variables.

plan.title: Goal setting
plan.detail: Record baseline WPM, set a term goal on the tracker. Aim for +8 WPM by December at 95% accuracy.

plan.title: Term map
plan.detail: Walk through the term plan and the deadline weeks. Log out.

successCriteria: I recorded my baseline WPM and set a goal.
I can explain what a loop and an if-block do.
I know what the term project requires.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Refresh Year 5 micro:bit basics: show icons, buttons, loops, conditions. Switch MakeCode to Python view — read the code aloud.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode (Blocks + Python view), micro:bit, Year 5 skills recap sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Rebuild the Year 5 basics: icons, buttons, loops, conditions.
Switch MakeCode to Python view and read the code aloud.
Match each block to its Python line.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Speed rebuild
plan.detail: Four mini-challenges in 15 minutes: show an icon, respond to a button, animate with a loop, react to shake. Everyone should manage at least three.

plan.title: Python view
plan.detail: Toggle to Python. Read the code aloud together, line by line. Point out: indentation matters, the colon at the end of a line, the def keyword.

plan.title: Match-up
plan.detail: Cut-up cards: match Blocks images to Python lines. Then predict what an unseen Python line will do before running it.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: What is the same in both views? What is easier about each? Log out.

successCriteria: I rebuilt at least three Year 5 programs.
I can read a Python line and say what it does.
I can match a block to its Python line.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Store a value in a variable ('score', 'name', 'temp'). Change it during the program. Display it on the LED matrix.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, printed variables reference (Blocks ⇆ Python). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Create a variable and give it a starting value.
Change a variable while the program runs.
Display a variable on the LED display.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a variable?
plan.detail: A labelled box that holds a value you can change. Physical demo: a box labelled 'score' with cards swapped in and out.

plan.title: Make a counter
plan.detail: set score to 0; on button A pressed, change score by 1; show number score. Test - this is the single most useful pattern of the term.

plan.title: Reset and limits
plan.detail: Add button B to reset the score to 0. Challenge: use an if-block so the score cannot go above 10.

plan.title: Python check
plan.detail: Toggle to Python: spot score = 0 and score += 1. Log out.

successCriteria: My program has a variable with a starting value.
The variable changes when I press a button.
The current value is shown on the display.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Bring loops and if-blocks together: a program that keeps checking the temperature and shows different faces at different thresholds.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, worked-example cards, first-time-teacher video: 'micro:bit temperature project' (Craig 'n Dave). TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Combine a loop with if / else if conditions.
Use a sensor reading to choose between three outcomes.
Test each branch of my program.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Three-way decisions
plan.detail: Walk through the worked example: cold below 25, warm 25-30, hot above 30. Draw the decision as a flowchart on the board.

plan.title: Build the thermometer
plan.detail: forever loop, read temperature, if/else if/else showing three different faces. Order matters - discuss why checking 'hot' first changes the behaviour.

plan.title: Test every branch
plan.detail: Cold: hold near the window or press a cold object to the chip. Hot: cup it in both hands. Every branch must be seen to work.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Why does the order of the conditions matter? Log out.

successCriteria: My program uses a loop and at least three branches.
I saw every branch work on the device.
I can explain why condition order matters.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Send messages between two micro:bits using the radio blocks. Build a 'ping-pong' game: A sends '1', B sends '2', repeat.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, 2 micro:bits per pair, radio-blocks reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Send and receive numbers between two micro:bits.
Build a two-device ping-pong game.
Explain why both devices need the same radio group.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Radio recap
plan.detail: Same group = same channel. Assign group numbers per pair. Both devices get the SAME program.

plan.title: Ping-pong build
plan.detail: On button A send 1; on received 1, show arrow and send 2 back; on received 2, show a different arrow. Watch the message bounce between devices.

plan.title: Add a counter
plan.detail: Add a variable that counts how many times the message has bounced. Links Week 3 to today.

plan.title: Debug together
plan.detail: Common faults: only one device flashed, group mismatch, infinite loop of messages. Log out.

successCriteria: Messages travel both ways between the devices.
My program uses a variable to count bounces.
I can fix a radio group mismatch.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Choose ONE project idea from a menu: fitness tracker, distance messenger, class attendance signaller, mini-quiz device. Plan on paper — features, inputs, outputs.
lessons.sowResources: Project menu card (4 options), planning sheet, MakeCode. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Choose a project and list its features.
Identify the inputs and outputs for each feature.
Produce a plan a partner could build from.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The project menu
plan.detail: Fitness tracker, distance messenger, attendance signaller, mini-quiz device. For each, discuss what would be hard and what would be satisfying.

plan.title: Feature thinking
plan.detail: A feature is one thing the device does for the user. Break each project idea into three features - this is the planning skill being assessed.

plan.title: Write the plan
plan.detail: Planning sheet: project name, who it is for, three features, inputs, outputs, variables needed.

plan.title: Swap and test the plan
plan.detail: Give your plan to another pair. Could they build from it? Clarify anything they questioned. Log out.

activities: Break the project into three features
successCriteria: My plan names three specific features.
I have listed the inputs, outputs and variables.
Another pair understood my plan.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Implement the first main feature. Save with clear file name (project_v1.hex). Test with a partner.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, class shared drive. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Implement the first feature of my project.
Test it before adding anything else.
Save the code as project_v1.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: One feature at a time
plan.detail: Rule for the build: get feature 1 working and saved before touching feature 2. Explain why - if everything breaks at once you cannot find the cause.

plan.title: Build feature 1
plan.detail: Independent build from the plan. Circulate and ask 'show me it working'. Keep a shared board of solutions to problems that come up more than once.

plan.title: Test and save
plan.detail: Partner tests feature 1 against the plan. Save as project_v1. Log out.

successCriteria: Feature 1 works on the physical device.
A partner tested it against my plan.
My code is saved as project_v1.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add a second feature to the build. Test again with a partner. Save as v2.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, version-control notes card. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add a second feature without breaking the first.
Re-test both features together.
Save as project_v2 and keep v1.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Why keep old versions?
plan.detail: If v2 breaks badly you can go back to v1. Show the version-control notes card. Professional habit, taught early.

plan.title: Build feature 2
plan.detail: Add the second feature. Re-test feature 1 afterwards - it often breaks, and noticing that is the learning.

plan.title: Test both and save
plan.detail: Test both features in one run. Save as project_v2. Log out.

successCriteria: Both features work in the same program.
I checked feature 1 still works.
I have v1 and v2 saved separately.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Practise explaining the whole program to a partner: what the variables do, where the loops are, what each if-block checks.
lessons.sowResources: Sentence-stem cards, peer-explanation rubric, TypingClub. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Explain my whole program to a partner.
Say what each variable holds and where it changes.
Identify every loop and condition in my code.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Model the explanation
plan.detail: Teacher explains a sample project well, then badly. Class scores both against the rubric so the standard is clear.

plan.title: Explain in pairs
plan.detail: Two rounds with feedback in between. The rubric rewards naming variables, loops and conditions specifically.

plan.title: Teacher questioning
plan.detail: One-to-one exam-style questions: 'What happens if the user presses B twice?', 'Where does the score get reset?'

plan.title: Target setting
plan.detail: Each pupil writes one thing to explain better next time. Log out.

successCriteria: I explained my program without reading the screen.
I named my variables and said what they hold.
I pointed out every loop and condition.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Debug 4 teacher-made 'broken' programs. Identify the bug, propose the fix, then apply and re-test.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, printed buggy-code sheets, teacher exemplar solutions. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Find the bug in a broken program.
Propose a fix before changing anything.
Apply the fix and re-test.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Debugging method
plan.detail: Read the code, predict what it should do, run it, compare, then change ONE thing. Predict-run-compare beats random clicking.

plan.title: Debug marathon
plan.detail: Four broken programs, 10 minutes each: a loop with no pause, a variable never reset, an if/else if in the wrong order, a radio group mismatch. Write the diagnosis before fixing.

plan.title: Solutions reveal
plan.detail: Compare with the exemplar solutions. Which bug was hardest to see and why? Log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a diagnosis before changing any code.
I fixed at least three of the four programs.
I can name a bug type I now recognise on sight.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Individual practical + oral: demo the project and explain the code. Assessed on features, loops, conditions, variables and explanation quality.
lessons.sowResources: Marking rubric — from HTML: 'a multi-feature micro:bit Python project, explained clearly to peers'.
objectives: Demonstrate my multi-feature project working.
Explain the code clearly to the teacher.
Show where variables, loops and conditions are used.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Assessment criteria on the board: features working, correct use of variables, loops, conditions, and quality of explanation.

plan.title: Final build time
plan.detail: Last chance to get features working. Silent conditions, technical help only.

plan.title: Demo and oral
plan.detail: One at a time: demo the device, then answer three questions about the code. Rest of the class continues polishing.

plan.title: Save the evidence
plan.detail: Final .hex saved with the correct name, plus a screenshot of the code.

plan.title: Close down
plan.detail: Devices counted in. Log out.

activities: Save code and screenshot as evidence
successCriteria: My project has at least two working features.
I used variables, a loop and a condition.
I explained the code without reading it out.
My evidence is saved correctly.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Add a third polish feature to the project (sound, animation, reset routine, welcome screen). Update the file to v3.
lessons.sowResources: MakeCode, micro:bit, feature-ideas menu. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Add a third feature that improves the user experience.
Keep the earlier features working.
Save the project as v3.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Polish that matters
plan.detail: From the feature-ideas menu: welcome screen, sound feedback, reset routine, low-battery warning. Choose based on what a real user would need.

plan.title: Build feature 3
plan.detail: Implement, then regression-test features 1 and 2.

plan.title: User test
plan.detail: Hand the device to someone who has never used it. Watch without helping. Note every hesitation.

plan.title: Save v3
plan.detail: Save and log the change in the dev diary. Log out.

successCriteria: My project has three working features.
The earlier features still work.
I watched a new user try it and noted what confused them.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Design a one-page poster (Docs / Slides) explaining what the project does, who it's for, and how it works. Include a photo of the device.
lessons.sowResources: Google Slides / PowerPoint, class camera, poster template. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Design a one-page poster explaining my project.
Say who the project is for and how it works.
Include a photo of the device.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What makes a good poster
plan.detail: Look at the template: title, what it does, who it is for, how it works, photo. Rule: a reader should understand it in 30 seconds.

plan.title: Photograph the device
plan.detail: Apply Year 3 photography rules: good light, in focus, off-centre framing. Take three, choose the best.

plan.title: Build the poster
plan.detail: In Slides or Docs: insert the photo, write short sections, keep text large. No walls of text.

plan.title: 30-second test
plan.detail: Partner reads your poster for 30 seconds then explains your project back. If they cannot, the poster needs work. Log out.

successCriteria: My poster explains what the project does and who it is for.
It includes a clear photo of my device.
A partner understood it in 30 seconds.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Rehearse a 3-minute presentation of the project. Peers give feedback: 'Was the code explanation clear?'.
lessons.sowResources: Presentation timer, peer-feedback sheet, class projector. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)

Explain the code section clearly.
Act on peer feedback before the showcase.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Rehearse in threes

plan.title: Act on the feedback
plan.detail: Adjust the poster or the script. Practise the weakest minute again.

plan.title: Timing check
plan.detail: Final run against the timer. Over-runners cut one sentence. Log out.

successCriteria: My presentation fits in three minutes.
My code explanation was rated clear by two peers.
I changed something based on the feedback.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Present projects to Year 5 (or another class). Save .hex + poster + demo photo to the portfolio folder. Ready for secondary!

objectives: Present my project to a younger audience.
Answer questions from visitors.
Save all my project evidence to the portfolio.

plan.title: Set up
plan.detail: Stations with device, poster and laptop showing the code. Invite Year 5 in.

plan.title: Project fair

plan.title: Feedback read

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save .hex, poster and device photo to the portfolio folder with correct names.

plan.title: Ready for secondary
plan.detail: Reflect: which skills carry into Year 7? Devices counted in. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented to visitors within the time.
I answered at least two questions about my project.
My .hex, poster and photo are in the portfolio folder.

plan.title: Goals and deadlines

I completed the diagnostic and saved it correctly.
I can describe the three files in the term project.

Type without looking at the keyboard.
Track my progress against the class average.

Generate and update an automatic Table of Contents.
Compare how Word and Docs handle styles.

plan.title: Styles properly

plan.title: Comparison table

successCriteria: My document uses modified styles, not manual formatting.
My contents list generates and updates automatically.
I can state two differences between Word and Docs.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Insert and format tables. Add captioned images. Add a short reference list using proper formatting.
lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, printed reference-formatting exemplar. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Insert and format a table to a brief.
Add captioned images with automatic numbering.
Format a short reference list consistently.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Tables to a brief
plan.detail: Given a specification (5 columns, header row, banded rows, no wrapped text), build it exactly. Following a brief precisely is the IGCSE skill being seeded.

plan.title: Captions and figures
plan.detail: Insert two images with automatic captions. Discuss caption style: what the figure shows, not 'a picture'.

plan.title: References
plan.detail: Model a simple reference format: Author (Year) Title, URL, date accessed. Add three references for sources used, formatted identically.

plan.title: Brief check
plan.detail: Swap and mark a partner's work against the written brief - tick or cross only, no opinions. Log out.

successCriteria: My table matches every point in the brief.
My images are captioned and numbered automatically.
My three references use exactly the same format.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Enter data with clear headings. Use =SUM, =AVERAGE, =MAX, =MIN. Format as a table with alternating row colours.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, formula reference card, sample class marks data. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Enter data with clear headings.
Use SUM, AVERAGE, MAX and MIN.
Format a range as a table with banded rows.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Anatomy of a spreadsheet
plan.detail: Cells, rows, columns, ranges. Rule: one heading row, one record per row, no blank rows in the middle.

plan.title: Four formulas
plan.detail: Enter the sample class marks data. Then =SUM(B2:B16), =AVERAGE, =MAX, =MIN. Show the colon meaning 'through' and dragging to select a range.

plan.title: Fill down
plan.detail: Use the fill handle to copy a formula down a column. Watch the cell references change - introduce the idea of relative references.

plan.title: Format as a table
plan.detail: Apply table formatting with banded rows and a bold header. Repeat the whole task in Google Sheets. Log out.

activities: SUM / AVERAGE / MAX / MIN on real data
successCriteria: My data has one clear heading row.
I used all four formulas correctly.
My range is formatted as a readable table.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Turn data into a bar and a pie chart. Add conditional formatting so scores > 80 are highlighted green.
lessons.sowResources: Excel · Sheets, chart-choice poster, conditional-formatting how-to. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Create a bar chart and a pie chart from the same data.
Choose the right chart type for the question.
Apply conditional formatting with a rule.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Which chart, and why
plan.detail: Bar for comparing amounts, pie for parts of a whole, line for change over time. Show a bad pie chart with 12 slices - the class will spot the problem.

plan.title: Build both charts
plan.detail: Select the range, insert a bar chart, then a pie chart. Add a title and axis labels - an unlabelled chart scores nothing.

plan.title: Conditional formatting
plan.detail: Rule: highlight scores above 80 in green, below 40 in red. Then change a value and watch the colour update live.

plan.title: Justify
plan.detail: Write one sentence: which chart answers the question better and why. Save both files. Log out.

successCriteria: My charts have titles and labelled axes.
I can justify my chart choice in one sentence.
My conditional formatting updates when data changes.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Design principles: 1 idea per slide, minimal text, big font, consistent theme. Build a 5-slide deck.
lessons.sowResources: Microsoft PowerPoint, Google Slides, printed design principles handout, Duarte 'Slidedocs' free reference. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Apply slide design principles: one idea per slide, minimal text.
Use a consistent theme.
Build a 5-slide deck.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Death by PowerPoint
plan.detail: Show a slide crammed with bullet points, then the same content across three clean slides. Rules: one idea per slide, 6 words per line where possible, 24pt minimum.

plan.title: Build the deck
plan.detail: Five slides: title, context, main point, evidence, conclusion. Apply a single theme throughout.

plan.title: Contrast and images
plan.detail: Check text contrast against backgrounds; use one full-bleed image rather than three small ones.

plan.title: Three-second test
plan.detail: Flash each slide for three seconds. Can a partner say what it is about? Save in both PowerPoint and Slides. Log out.

successCriteria: Each slide covers one idea.
My deck uses a single consistent theme.
A partner understood each slide in three seconds.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Save to Drive and OneDrive. Share a file with 'Comment' vs 'Edit' rights. Collaborate live with a partner on the same file.
lessons.sowResources: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, sharing-permissions cheat sheet. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
objectives: Save files to both Drive and OneDrive.
Share a file with Comment rather than Edit rights.
Collaborate live on one document.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Permissions matter
plan.detail: View, Comment, Edit - what each allows. Discuss a real scenario: sharing homework with a friend. Which permission, and why? Touches digital citizenship directly.

plan.title: Share and check
plan.detail: Share a document with a partner as Comment-only. The partner tries to edit and cannot - proof the permission works.

plan.title: Live collaboration
plan.detail: Change to Edit and both type in the same document simultaneously. Observe cursors, name labels and version history.

plan.title: Version history
plan.detail: Open version history and restore an earlier version. Powerful safety net - show it explicitly. Log out.

successCriteria: My file is saved in both Drive and OneDrive.
I shared a file with the correct permission level.
I co-edited a document and found version history.

lessons.subject: ICT
lessons.outline: Start the linked mini-project: a Report (Word / Docs) + a Spreadsheet (Excel / Sheets) + a Deck (PPT / Slides) on ONE topic. Plan today.

objectives: Choose one topic that works across all three files.
Plan the report, spreadsheet and deck together.
Identify what data I need to collect.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: One topic, three files
plan.detail: Read the project brief. The three files must connect: the spreadsheet data appears as a chart in the report and in the deck. Show the teacher exemplar set.

plan.title: Topic selection
plan.detail: Topic must have numbers - screen time, canteen prices, sports results, travel to school. Reject topics with no data to chart.

plan.title: Plan all three
plan.detail: Planning sheet with three columns: report sections, spreadsheet columns and rows, slide titles. Plan them together so they line up.

plan.title: Data collection plan
plan.detail: Decide how to get 15+ rows of data before Week 13 - survey, measurement or published source. Log out.

successCriteria: My topic has numerical data I can chart.
My plan covers the report, spreadsheet and deck.
I know how I will collect at least 15 rows of data.

Peer-check work against the rubric.
Identify my weakest skill and practise it.

plan.detail: Structure an unformatted text with styles and generate a contents list, against the clock.

plan.title: Station 2 - Chart in Sheets
plan.detail: From a given dataset: build a labelled chart and apply conditional formatting.

plan.title: Station 3 - Deck in Slides
plan.detail: Build three well-designed slides from supplied content.

plan.title: Station 4 - Cloud share
plan.detail: Save to both clouds with correct names and share with the right permission.

plan.title: Peer check and target
plan.detail: Peer-mark one station against the rubric. Write your weakest skill as a target. Log out.

successCriteria: I completed all four stations in the time.
I marked a peer's work accurately against the rubric.
I have named the skill I need to practise.

lessons.subject: ICT

Work across Microsoft and Google tools.
Save everything to the cloud with correct names.

plan.title: Brief
plan.detail: Read the task twice. 90 minutes, three files, one topic. Rubric visible. Silent conditions.

plan.title: Spreadsheet first
plan.detail: Data, formulas, chart. Doing this first means the chart is ready to embed - remind them of this strategy.

plan.title: Report
plan.detail: Structured with styles, a contents list, the embedded chart and a captioned image.

plan.title: Deck
plan.detail: Three slides: title, findings with the chart, conclusion.

plan.title: Save and submit
plan.detail: All three files saved to the cloud with the correct names, in the assessment folder.

successCriteria: All three files are on the same topic.
My spreadsheet has formulas and a labelled chart.
My report is structured with a contents list.
Everything is saved to the cloud correctly named.

lessons.sowResources: Word · Docs, project brief. TypingClub warm-up (5-10 min every lesson)
